name: nerve injury overview
title: Nerve injury: after ruling out a tendon or blood-flow cause, localize the lesion (radiculopathy versus mononeuropathy) from the pattern of sensory loss and weakness, then grade it by the Seddon classification (neurapraxia, axonotmesis, neurotmesis), which predicts recovery; electrodiagnostic studies confirm, localize and grade

root.title: Numbness, tingling or weakness: is it a NERVE, WHERE is it, HOW BAD is it?
lines: first exclude a tendon (weakness) or poor blood flow (numbness) · TRUE sensory loss is always neurogenic: central or peripheral?
negative symptoms: numbness, weakness, lost reflexes · positive: pain, paresthesia (tingling)

groups.title: WHERE: root or named nerve?
lines: the map of the numbness and WHICH muscles are weak decide

groups.title: HOW BAD: Seddon grade
lines: which layer is cut decides recovery

head: h
Radiculopathy
spinal nerve ROOT
compressed in the intervertebral foramen
clue: Neck or back pain radiating down the limb
• eased by taking tension off (arm overhead)
tx: C6 dermatome: lateral arm, forearm, thumb
gluteus medius, tibialis posterior, paraspinals also abnormal

head: h
Mononeuropathy
one NAMED nerve
compressed at a typical site
clue: • weak in THAT nerve's muscles only
• not same-root muscles of other nerves
tx: at the fibular head: dorsiflexion, toe extension, eversion 0/5

head: h
Axonotmesis
AXON cut, EPINEURIUM intact
crush, stretch
clue: axon beyond the injury breaks down
inv: EMG: denervation at rest, few or no motor units
tx: • 1 mm a day = 1 inch a month

head: h
Neurotmesis
EPINEURIUM cut
nerve discontinuous
inv: only recovery, or none, tells them apart
tx: refer: peripheral nerve injury clinic (physiatry or plastics)

panels.title: Electrodiagnostic studies (EDX) = nerve conduction studies (NCS) + needle electromyography (EMG)
items: NCS: SIZE of the response = axon health · SPEED = myelin health
EMG: is the muscle quiet at rest (denervated muscle is not)? does it fire on command? which muscle exactly?
Answers: is it a nerve, where, how bad (myelin or axon, in continuity?), the likely timeline, or a muscle problem (myopathy)
NOT for musculoskeletal pain (rotator cuff tear) or central nervous system disease (stroke)
